items.title: 【Claude Fable 5.2 の effort を high から max に上げたら、トークンも時間も約4倍、見つけたバグの数は同じでした】
items.summary:
【Claude Fable 5.2 の effort を high から max に上げたら、トークンも時間も約4倍、見つけたバグの数は同じでした】

high・xhigh・max の3つで同じ問題を解かせた、自前の実験の結果です

Claude Codeには「effort（エフォート）」という設定があります
AIにどれだけ念入りに作業させるかを選ぶ物で、上げるほどトークンも時間もかかります

max は、トークンの消費が半端ないです
普段から max にしている人は、少ないと思います

では、その分だけ結果は良くなるのか
そこを確かめました

先に結果を書きます

・見つけたバグの数は、3つとも同じでした（全部見つけてます）
・変わったのはトークンと時間で、max は high の約4倍
・細かい所の質は、上の設定の方が少し良かった
・費用と質のバランスが一番良かったのは、真ん中の xhigh

ただ、各設定2回ずつの小さな実験です
「max は無駄」とまでは言えません
その理由も書きます

▼どうやって比べたか

問題は、別の会社のAIに作らせました
OpenAIの GPT-6 Astra です

Claudeの系統のAIが出題すると、Claudeが見落としやすい所と重なって、甘い試験になるからです

仕込んだバグは、全部プログラムを実際に動かして、本物だと確かめてあります

解く側は、Claude Codeを画面なしで自動実行して、ファイルを読む道具だけを使わせました

採点は、誰の答えかを伏せた上で、GPT-6 Astra と Claude Opus 5.5 が別々にやってます
解く側が正解表を一度も読んでいない事も、実行の記録で確かめました

同じ問題を設定ごとに2回ずつ、全部で24回です

▼まず、普通の難しさで

ECサイトの決済のコードに、バグを10個仕込みました
「正しいのに怪しく見える」ひっかけも3個入れてます

結果は、3つとも10個全部を発見
ひっかけを間違って指摘した回数もゼロでした

障害の原因を当てる問題も、3つとも正解です

これでは差が分からないので、難しくして作り直しました

▼次に、かなり難しくして

約750行のコードに、バグを14個
ひっかけは5個です

14個のうち4個は、出題したAIが「熟練者が1回読んで見つけられるのは30%程度」と見込んだ物でした
夏時間に切り替わる日の時刻の比較や、同時に書き込んだ時の失敗などです

もう1問は、543行の生のログから障害の原因を突き止める問題
2台のサーバーの時計が約87秒ずれていて、答えをまとめた行は1行もありません

それでも、3つとも14個全部を発見
ログの問題も、採点した8項目が全部正解でした

3つの中で一番軽い high が、2回とも全部見抜いてます

▼違ったのは、トークンと時間

難しくした方のコードの問題、1回あたりの数字です

・high　出力 約2.3万トークン、約4.2分
・xhigh　出力 約5.1万トークン、約8.8分
・max　出力 約10.9万トークン、約18分

max は high と比べて、トークンが約4.7倍、時間が約4.3倍です
問題によって幅があって、トークンは約3.6〜4.7倍、時間は約3.5〜4.3倍でした

トークンは、AIが読み書きする量の単位です
料金や使用量の元になります

APIの定価に直すと、1回あたり high が約1.2ドル、xhigh が約2.4ドル、max が約5.0ドルでした
定額のプランなら、この金額が請求されるわけではないです

▼差が出たのは、細かい所

1つ目は、バグの深刻さの付け方です
正解表と合っていた割合は、平均で high が約58%、xhigh が約72%、max が約77%でした

2つ目は、ログを引用する時の正確さです
引用の誤りは、全体で high が9件、xhigh が5件、max が3件でした（GPT-6 Astraの判定）

ただ、xhigh と max の差は小さいです
深刻さの付け方は、普通の難しさの方では max、難しくした方では xhigh の方が合っていて、順番が入れ替わってます

▼やってみて面白かった事

max だけ、読み直しが増えてました
ログの問題で、ファイルを読むなどのやり取りは、high と xhigh が16回、max が25回です
それでも、結論の正しさは変わりませんでした

もう1つは、採点するAIにも好みが出た事です
答えの中に「9月にも同じ問題が起きていたはず」という、証拠から一歩踏み込んだ推測がありました
Claudeは役に立つ警告として加点して、GPT-6 Astraは根拠を超えた推測として減点してます

▼この実験で言えない事

・各設定2回ずつ、全部で24回の小さな実験です
・問題は人工的に作った物なので、実際のコード全部に当てはまるとは限りません
・難しくしても high が満点だったので、「max でないと解けない難しさ」は測れていません
・深刻さの正解は、出題したAI 1つの判断です
・時間は、3〜6本を同時に動かした時の値です（3つは常に同時に動かしたので、比べる条件はそろってます）
・high より下の設定は、比べていません

なので「max は無駄」とは言えません
言えるのは、「この問題では、設定を上げても見つかる数は増えなかった」までです

正直、「max は無駄でした」と言い切った方が伸びると思います
でも、そこまで言える実験ではないので言いません

▼公式の説明とも合ってました

Anthropicの公式の説明では、effort は「考える深さ」だけの設定ではないです
返答の文章にも、ファイルを読むなどの道具の呼び出しにも、考える量にも影響する、とされてます

max だけ読み直しが増えたのは、この説明と合ってます

Claude Codeの公式の説明には、max は効果が頭打ちになる事があって、考え過ぎる傾向があるので、広く使う前に試すように、とも書かれてます

今回は、それを自分の問題で確かめた形です

▼来そうな質問に先に答えておきます

「じゃあ high で十分？」
→ 見つける数は同じでしたが、深刻さの付け方や引用の正確さは、上の設定の方が少し良かったです
いつも high で良い、とは言えません

「定額のプランなら、トークンは気にしなくていい？」
→ 金額は請求されませんが、時間は約4倍かかります
公式の説明でも、effort を上げるほど使用量の上限に早く届く、とされてます

「AIが作った問題を、AIが採点して意味がある？」
→ そこは弱い所です
なので、出題と採点を別の会社のAIにして、誰の答えかを伏せました
バグが本物かどうかは、プログラムを動かして確かめてあります

▼まとめ

・Claude Fable 5.2 の effort を、high・xhigh・max で比べた（全24回）
・見つけたバグの数は、3つとも同じ
・max は high の約4倍のトークンと時間がかかった
・細かい所の質は上の設定が少し良く、バランスは xhigh が一番良かった
・小さな実験なので、「max は無駄」とは言えない

「ここは max でないと駄目だった」という場面があれば、教えてください

items.title: Why is Nvidia so powerful in the AI world, and what could Jensen Huang’s scandal really cost?
items.summary:
The AI sector is notorious for the amount of circular financing going on – where companies invest in their own suppliers or customers. Nvidia is a key player in this loop.

Investors are already fretting over whether the enormous amounts of money sunk into AI can ever return profits.

While leading AI model builders Anthropic and OpenAI are moving toward public listings or fresh funding rounds, both face harsh reality checks. [...] The now multi-trillion-dollar company got its start making chips called graphic processing units (GPUs), used largely for video games. However, these chips – and their successors – turned out to be ideal for the kind of number-crunching needed for training and using AI models.

Other companies such as Google and AMD have tried to make chips that can compete with Nvidia for speed and efficiency, however neither has been able to displace Nvidia from its dominance of the AI market. [...] Computer chips – specifically the chips used to produce and run artificial intelligence (AI) systems – have become a key front in the United States’ rivalry with China for geopolitical power and influence. The most powerful chips are needed for the most advanced AI, and the US has tried to maintain its edge over China by restricting access to those chips.

While the Chinese government rejects claims of espionage, Alice Huang has reportedly been under investigation by the US for years.

items.title: GPT-5 Shows Substantial Agreement in Interpreting Ultrasound Cochrane
items.summary: When compared to the consensus reference standard, GPT-5 demonstrated varying levels of agreement across the different variables. The model showed the highest agreement for review purpose, with 88.9% exact agreement and a Cohen’s kappa of 0.793. For evidence certainty, the model achieved 70.4% exact agreement, with a quadratic weighted kappa of 0.782, indicating substantial agreement when accounting for the ordinal nature of the certainty scale. [...] A new descriptive meta-research study published in BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making evaluates the performance of the GPT-5 API in structurally interpreting ultrasound-related Cochrane reviews. The research, conducted by a team including Weizao Wu, Anchen Liu, and colleagues, aims to clarify the role of ultrasound within systematic reviews and assess the field-specific capabilities of large language models in evidence synthesis. By combining a two-level analysis of review topics with [...] To evaluate the GPT-5 API, the researchers employed a structured extraction process targeting four key variables: review purpose, clinical domain, evidence certainty, and conclusion polarity. Two independent clinicians annotated the focused subset of 54 reviews while blinded to the GPT-5 outputs. Disagreements between the human reviewers were resolved through consensus adjudication, creating a final operational reference standard against which the AI’s performance was measured.

items.title: Why is Nvidia so powerful in the AI world, and what could Jensen Huang’s scandal really cost?
items.summary:
The AI sector is notorious for the amount of circular financing going on – where companies invest in their own suppliers or customers. Nvidia is a key player in this loop.

Investors are already fretting over whether the enormous amounts of money sunk into AI can ever return profits.

While leading AI model builders Anthropic and OpenAI are moving toward public listings or fresh funding rounds, both face harsh reality checks. [...] The now multi-trillion-dollar company got its start making chips called graphic processing units (GPUs), used largely for video games. However, these chips – and their successors – turned out to be ideal for the kind of number-crunching needed for training and using AI models.

Other companies such as Google and AMD have tried to make chips that can compete with Nvidia for speed and efficiency, however neither has been able to displace Nvidia from its dominance of the AI market. [...] Computer chips – specifically the chips used to produce and run artificial intelligence (AI) systems – have become a key front in the United States’ rivalry with China for geopolitical power and influence. The most powerful chips are needed for the most advanced AI, and the US has tried to maintain its edge over China by restricting access to those chips.

While the Chinese government rejects claims of espionage, Alice Huang has reportedly been under investigation by the US for years.

items.title: Dusting off this tweet from April because this gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is *widening*. It's now les
items.summary:
Dusting off this tweet from April because this gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is *widening*. It's now less "two groups of people speaking past each other" and more a sharp funnel.

- Napkin math somewhere around 6B people (~75% of the population) have barely come in contact with LLMs at all.
- Around 1-2B (~20%) are casual and infrequent users of free-tier ChatGPT-like products. This group sees derpy chatbots and treats them a bit like a better Google search, a writing aid, or etc. Maybe an agent tries to book you a flight. I have non-tech friends who (reasonably, imo) say they have not much use for it at all. Even many professionals outside of math&code are in this tier. For example, execs and many other functions spend a lot of their time talking to other people, so while they understand what is happening intellectually, it is still second-hand and a bit abstract.
- Now we get to professional use of frontier-grade LLMs in math&code. Somewhere around 20M people (0.2%) see first-hand that large, complex projects that used to take them weeks/months can now be completed by agents with a prompt. Building apps, copying apps, translating apps, decompiling apps from binaries... This has all happened very quickly and recently - less than 1 year ago, I was writing code manually by hand, typing memorized computer code commands into a code editor character by character, occasionally pressing Tab to autocomplete a little chunk of code.
- And finally we get to the ~5,000 people (~0.00006%) with access to frontier-grade systems internally. The external world has seen the preview. It looks like swarms of thousands of agents collaborating over weeks on software mega projects: minting zero days, running cyber attacks and defenses at machine speeds, discovering new science, advancing the frontier of mathematics. Things that would have taken top professionals in the industry years of work. Meanwhile, human review and comprehension are starting to fall behind. For example, people are still involved in the "archeology" of the OpenAI-HF incident from many months ago. Mathematicians may be poring over the 722 manuscripts on frontier mathematics for a while.

The funnel is driven by a combination of factors:
1. The impact scales with ambition, problem size, and horizon. A question with a paragraph answer barely stresses the system. You need a reservoir of big, difficult problems that you really care about. This aspect drives the consumer / professional dimension of the funnel.
2. The jaggedness of the system (which I have written about a lot separately). Capability peaks in domains that are digital, verifiable and economically valuable. This is because LLM capability emerges from reinforcement learning on verifiable rewards on a curated environment mixture driven by revenue potential. This aspect primarily drives the area (e.g. math&code) dimension of the funnel.
3. Access. Free-tier, paid-tier, internal.

So this is the weirdness of the moment. The general public has mostly not interacted with these systems. When they have, it looks like a derpy chatbot. The majority of professionals still see only a modest uplift. And a small sliver of professionals are experiencing the vertigo of the curve going vertical. And it is all happening at the same time.

SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 5 (Reuters) - Stunning ​victories by Democrats in US midterm elections this week have been interpreted by many as Americans repudiating tech ‌industry plans to build data centers across the country. OpenAI has now embarked on new strategies to change their minds.

The AI lab on Thursday laid out policies — in the works since August — intended to help the company build more trust with local communities and convince them that data centers will ​benefit them. [...] OpenAI officials, along with many of their peers in tech, ​have spent the last ⁠two years trying to build ties with the administration of US President Donald Trump in hopes of shaping federal policy around AI.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman donated $1 million to Trump's inaugural committee and later attended Trump's second inauguration. Last year, Brockman donated $25 million in his personal capacity to ⁠a Trump ​super PAC.

items.title: OpenAI employees warned about operational security lapses for years, sources say | Reuters
items.summary:
OpenAI and Anthropic have tried to ​maintain a more open research culture to both ⁠attract employees and foster creativity that can lead to breakthroughs. The AI field is rooted in academia, where machine-learning scientists have openly discussed their research.

Some OpenAI employees are increasingly worried about this approach as AI grows more capable, according to the five people. [...] When asked about employees' concerns and their view that management did not act on these issues, OpenAI spokesperson Elana Widmann ​said that OpenAI is one of the most targeted organizations in the world. As a result, the company invests heavily in its security program to protect against attacks from insiders, cybercriminals and nation-states, she said. These workers argued that OpenAI's controls were so lax ‌that outsiders, including foreign governments, could obtain sensitive information about the AI lab's technology with relative ease, the people said. For example, anybody at OpenAI who could access its code could see the technical details underlying many company projects.
